Chrzanow New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chrzanów, Poland

Not demolished. Established beside Chrzanów's original cemetery after an additional land purchase (both sharing a common wall from the early 19th century), this larger cemetery served a Jewish community that reached 6,328 residents by 1921, including descendants of the tzadik Diwrej Chaim (Chaim ben Arje Lejb Halberstam) and figures like cantor Hirsz Lejb Bakon and London-based Polish government member Ignacy Schwarzbart. During WWII, the cemetery held executions and ghetto burials, including a mass grave of 37 Chrzanów Jews murdered at Trzebinia in September 1939. Postwar Communist-era neglect (1945-1973) saw the watchman's house and funeral home demolished and the wall pulled down, though the site survived the war itself in relatively good condition. A thorough 2005-2007 restoration, led by the Jewish community and local authorities, repaired the wall and ohels, re-erected fallen stelae, and inventoried about 1,500 tombstones. Leaders of the Halbersztam Hasidic dynasty, including Dawid (d. 1894) and his sons, are buried in the southern ohel; Shlomo Bochner, a student of the Rebbe of Leżajsk, rests in the northern one. Vandalism in 2009 damaged about 50 stelae.
